question: Which gastric cells secrete hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor?
explanation: Parietal cells in the gastric glands produce both hydrochloric acid for digestion and intrinsic factor for vitamin B12 absorption. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h1)

question: What is the primary function of pepsinogen secreted by chief cells?
explanation: Pepsinogen is converted by hydrochloric acid into pepsin, which breaks down proteins in the stomach. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h1)

question: The most common bacterial cause of chronic gastritis is:
explanation: Helicobacter pylori colonizes the gastric mucosa and is responsible for the vast majority of chronic gastritis and peptic ulcer cases. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h2)

question: How does mucosal barrier breakdown lead to tissue damage in gastritis?

options.A: Bile salts accumulate and block the pyloric sphincter
options.B: Acid and pepsin diffuse back into the mucosal tissue
options.C: Gastrin suppresses the normal production of digestive enzymes
options.D: Intrinsic factor production increases beyond normal limits

explanation: Once the protective mucous layer is disrupted, gastric acid and pepsin damage the underlying tissue directly. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h2)

question: A life-threatening complication where an ulcer creates a hole in the stomach wall is:
explanation: Perforation occurs when an ulcer penetrates completely through the wall, spilling contents into the peritoneal cavity and causing an acute abdomen. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h3)

question: Pain from a duodenal ulcer is most likely to show which pattern?

options.A: Remains constant throughout the day regardless of meals
options.B: Increases immediately after eating any type of fatty food
options.C: Worsens when the stomach is empty and improves after eating
options.D: Appears only during the night and resolves by morning

explanation: Food buffers the acid temporarily in duodenal ulcers, so pain often occurs when the stomach is empty and food is consumed. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h3)

question: The most common histological type of gastric cancer is:
explanation: Gastric adenocarcinoma originates in the glandular cells of the gastric mucosa and represents over ninety percent of all stomach cancers. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h4)

question: Why is gastric cancer frequently diagnosed at an advanced stage?

options.A: Diagnostic blood tests detect tumor markers very late
options.B: Early stages of the disease are typically asymptomatic
options.C: Metastasis to the liver occurs before primary tumor formation
options.D: Symptoms mimic common acute gastritis in all patients

explanation: Because early gastric lesions cause few or no symptoms, patients usually seek care only after the tumor has grown or metastasized. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h4)

question: What is considered the gold standard diagnostic test for viewing gastric mucosal lesions?
explanation: EGD allows direct visualization of the stomach lining and permits tissue biopsy for definitive diagnosis. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h5)

question: Why is a Complete Blood Count commonly ordered for a patient with chronic PUD?

options.A: To check for anemia caused by slow, continuous blood loss
options.B: To measure the exact level of circulating gastric acid
options.C: To determine the presence of active bacterial infection
options.D: To evaluate liver function affected by poor fat digestion

explanation: Bleeding ulcers cause chronic blood loss, leading to iron-deficiency anemia which shows up on a CBC as low hemoglobin and hematocrit. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h5)

question: Which medication class directly blocks the final step of gastric acid secretion?
explanation: Proton pump inhibitors inhibit the hydrogen-potassium ATPase pump in parietal cells, effectively halting acid production. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of combining antibiotics with a PPI in PUD management?

options.A: Neutralizing excess acid in the duodenum
options.B: Stimulating the production of intrinsic factor
options.C: Creating a protective barrier over ulcers

explanation: Antibiotics target the underlying bacterial infection, while the PPI aids healing by reducing acid while the antibiotics work. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h6)

question: What is a primary nursing responsibility regarding a nasogastric tube after gastric surgery?

options.A: Keep the tube patent and avoid unprescribed repositioning
options.B: Advance the tube further into the duodenum to aid feeding
options.C: Irrigate the tube vigorously every two hours with sterile water
options.D: Remove the tube immediately if the patient reports nausea

explanation: Manipulating or repositioning an NG tube after gastric surgery can disrupt surgical anastomoses and cause hemorrhage or leakage. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h7)

question: Why might a surgeon perform a vagotomy during ulcer surgery?

options.A: To widen the pyloric sphincter and improve food emptying
options.B: To reduce gastric acid secretion by cutting nerve impulses
options.C: To bypass an obstruction caused by chronic scar tissue
options.D: To remove cancerous tissue located in the fundus of the stomach

explanation: A vagotomy cuts branches of the vagus nerve, decreasing vagal stimulation to parietal cells and thus lowering acid production. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h7)

question: Which symptom is characteristic of dumping syndrome after gastric surgery?

options.A: Marked hypertension immediately following heavy meals
options.B: Persistent high fever linked to peritoneal infection
options.C: Dizziness and sweating after rapid gastric emptying
options.D: Severe constipation caused by delayed intestinal transit

explanation: Dumping syndrome occurs when food moves too quickly from the stomach to the small intestine, causing vasomotor and gastrointestinal symptoms. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h8)

question: What dietary advice should a nurse give to help prevent dumping syndrome?

options.A: Drink plenty of fluids during meals to help digestion
options.B: Eat small, frequent meals and separate liquids from solids
options.C: Avoid all proteins and focus solely on high-carbohydrate diets
options.D: Consume large meals rich in simple sugars for quick energy

explanation: Smaller meals and avoiding fluids with food slow down gastric emptying and reduce the severity of dumping syndrome symptoms. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T6#GNS213_U3_T6_h8)
